suggestions.rationale: This catalog identity is specifically scoped to prolactin-secreting pituitary dysfunction. In men with prolactinoma, elevated prolactin can suppress the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis and larger tumors can additionally impair gonadotroph function by mass effect, producing hypogonadotropic hypogonadism. This supports an endocrine secondary pathway when hyperprolactinemia/prolactinoma and biochemical-clinical hypogonadism are documented with compatible chronology; it does not justify generalizing the relationship to unrelated forms of hyperpituitarism or attributing every low testosterone result to prolactin excess.

pathwayIntelligence.causalChain: Prolactin-secreting pituitary dysfunction with sustained hyperprolactinemia and/or tumor mass effect → suppression or impairment of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis → clinically confirmed hypogonadism.
developmentQuestions: Is the primary pituitary disorder documented as prolactin-secreting dysfunction or prolactinoma with sustained hyperprolactinemia?
Is hypogonadism clinically and biochemically confirmed rather than inferred from a single low testosterone result?
Do LH/FSH, testosterone, prolactin, and other pituitary-hormone results support central hypogonadism compatible with the pituitary disorder?
What is the chronology of prolactin elevation, tumor burden, gonadal symptoms, and biochemical hypogonadism?
Did gonadal-axis function improve after prolactin control or tumor treatment, and if not, is persistent pituitary damage documented?
Which medication, obesity, systemic-illness, sleep, testicular, aging, or other endocrine contributors should be addressed?
issuesToResolve: The mapping is limited to the repository's prolactin-secreting pituitary phenotype and should not be generalized to every form of hyperpituitarism.
Individual diagnosis requires compatible pituitary/gonadal laboratory findings, chronology, and assessment of alternative causes of hypogonadism.

evidenceGaps: Serial prolactin results and pituitary imaging or other records establishing prolactin-secreting pituitary dysfunction
Symptoms/signs plus repeated biochemical testing confirming hypogonadism
LH, FSH, testosterone and other clinically relevant pituitary-hormone testing
Treatment history and gonadal-axis response after prolactin control or tumor therapy
Endocrinology assessment of alternative causes and the individual endocrine relationship

sourceReferences.citation: Rudman Y, Shimon I. Hypogonadism in men with prolactinoma: Diagnosis, treatment, and management of persistent hypogonadism. Vitam Horm. 2025;129:185-202. PMID 40812946
sourceReferences.note: Clinical review describes hypogonadism as a common prolactinoma complication and identifies both prolactin-mediated suppression of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis and tumor mass effect as mechanisms. Supports a prolactinoma-specific endocrine pathway in men, not generic hyperpituitarism or automatic individual attribution.
sourceReferences.sourceLocator: PMID 40812946; abstract: most men with prolactinoma present with hypogonadism; mechanisms include prolactin-mediated HPG-axis suppression and tumor mass effect; >20% may remain hypogonadal after prolactin normalization
